calls.head: Power vs. Power
calls.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Aho’s line (Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Blackhawks’ first line is Kantserov, Bedard and Bertuzzi.

calls.head: Expect the Hurricanes to have the puck more
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina an 80% chance, and they delivered.

CHI.head: We gave Chicago only a 20% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Spencer Knight got lit up
surprises.body: Knight allowed 6 goals on 17 shots, worth 2.4 expected goals: 3.6 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 80 starts.

story.head: The Hurricanes hang 9 on the Blackhawks
paras: An ugly night for the Blackhawks. The first period belonged to the Hurricanes. Seth Jarvis and Jackson Blake scored less than two minutes apart early in the period to put the Canes up 2-0. Jordan Martinook stretched the lead to 3-0 midway through the period, and he scored again late in the period to make it 4-0. The second was all Hurricanes: Andrei Svechnikov scored, Sebastian Aho scored, and Alexander Nikishin scored, in his first game of the season, to make it 7-0. Chicago pulled Spencer Knight after six goals and turned to Arvid Söderblom for the rest of the second. The third period was a wild one. Roman Kantserov got the Blackhawks on the board early in the period, his fourth straight game with a goal. Connor Bedard cut Carolina’s lead to 7-2 with a little over six minutes left, but by then the game was long gone. Shayne Gostisbehere pushed the lead to 8-2 with less than four minutes left, and Svechnikov scored again with 13 seconds left to make it 9-2. Aho finished with a goal and two assists.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Hurricanes win about seven in ten. Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves for the Hurricanes. By our Swing measure, Sean Walker had the best night of anyone.

Only one penalty was called all night, something the league sees about once every 90 games. The Hurricanes improved to 14-3-2, still first in the NHL in both points and points percentage, while the Blackhawks dropped to 4-13-1, still last in the Central.
